subject: GCP private offer — list price escrow, reseller split & billing flow
messages:
From: Michelle Yang <m.yang@blueskylogistics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@blueskylogistics.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Private offer on GCP — target list-price & partner split

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo earlier — team is excited. We need to get a GCP Private Offer in place to move forward with a 12-month committed purchase. A few asks from procurement:

- Target effective discount off list: 30% on compute/embedding SKU lines for year-1.
- Require reseller/reseller-partner split to be documented (BlueSky will be reselling to sub-customers).
- Need to understand how Redwood plans to set the public list price vs the private offer execution (they want to avoid downstream channel confusion).
- We need sample contract terms + billing flow (GCP will invoice BlueSky or end-customer?).

Can you share the private-offer price matrix and confirm if you support list-price escrow (so the public SKU stays at list and the private offer applies as an off-invoice discount)? Also looping procurement here for any compliance questions.

Thanks,
Michelle
Michelle Yang
Head of Cloud Partnerships
BlueSky Logistics

-----
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Yang <m.yang@blueskylogistics.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 20:06:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Private offer on GCP — target list-price & partner split

Hi Michelle — great to hear you want to proceed. Short answers up front, details below and attached: redwood_gcp_price_matrix.xlsx + gcp_po_terms_v2.pdf.

- We can do a private offer on GCP with an off-invoice private discount (GCP private pricing model) while preserving the public SKU list price — we often call this a list-price+private discount pattern; GCP handles the private offer mapping so public catalog is unchanged.
- On partner/reseller splits: Redwood can designate BlueSky as the reseller on the PO. We do not move money off-platform; instead the partner margin is handled as an ARR-backed commission we recognize separately (Redwood -> BlueSky) or via marketplace-enabled partner settlement depending on your preference and GCP rules.

Proposed commercial starting point (internal guidance):
- Base private-offer discount to end-customer: 25% list (this is Redwood's standard floor for self-serve private offers).
- Partner reseller split (commission to BlueSky): 18% of list revenue (paid monthly after usage realization).
- For your 30% target, we can bridge the 5% delta two ways: Redwood increases discount to 28% with a protected margin clause, or Redwood stays at 25% + BlueSky takes a 5% uplift (i.e., 23% partner split). Both require executive approval for the extra erosion.

Next steps I recommend: Rafael (rev ops) to confirm maximum allowable off-invoice discount for a GCP private offer and Vanessa (channel ops) to outline partner settlement path and DocuSign workflow. I'll ask both to weigh in.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Private offer on GCP — target list-price & partner split

Thanks for looping me in. A few guardrails from rev ops/finance: we generally cannot exceed 25% off list on GCP private offers without an approved margin exception (exec-signed and with a deal-level simulator showing NPV).

Guidance:
- Standard maximum off-invoice private-offer discount: 25% (no approvals required).
- Max discount with VP+ signoff: 30% (requires a one-time margin exception form; finance will run a forecast).
- Partner commissions should be modeled on list price, not on net after private-offer discount — that preserves economic clarity for the partner.

To reach Michelle's 30% ask we can do:
Option A: Redwood sets private offer discount = 25%; BlueSky receives 5% uplift as reseller commission (i.e., partner split = 23% of list; Redwood keeps the balance).
Option B: Approve 30% private discount (requires VP signoff); partner commission stays at 18% of list.

I'm attaching the price matrix and a simple margin waterfall in the workbook. Rafael

-----
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Yang <m.yang@blueskylogistics.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:50:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Private offer on GCP — partner settlement and DocuSign flow

Hi Michelle — looping the ops details. Quick summary:

- We support two settlement flows for GCP private offers:
  1) Marketplace settlement: GCP invoices BlueSky and GCP remits to Redwood; partner commission then flows through GCP marketplace settlement tooling (subject to GCP fees and timing).
  2) Direct settlement with Redwood: GCP invoices BlueSky (or end-customer) at list, private-offer discount applied off-invoice; Redwood invoices BlueSky monthly for partner commission (we issue an invoice and pay the commission net of chargebacks).

- Recommended for speed: Marketplace settlement keeps everything on-platform but adds a ~2-3 week lag for partner payouts and a GCP fee (~1-2% of transacted value). Direct settlement is faster for partner cash flow but requires BlueSky to accept Redwood invoicing and an off-platform commission payment flow.

Attachments: gcp_po_terms_v2.pdf (term sheet), redwood_gcp_price_matrix.xlsx (price & waterfall). I also prepared a DocuSign envelope template we can use for the private-offer SOW (link shared above).

If you want me to draft the private-offer values: we propose starting the private offer with a 25% off list, partner split 18% of list, and a 6-month review for consumption-to-commit true-ups. If BlueSky needs the full 30% off list visible, Rafael's option B (exec signoff) is the path.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Operations Manager — Redwood Inference

-----
From: Michelle Yang <m.yang@blueskylogistics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private offer on GCP — list price escrow, reseller split & billing flow

Thanks all — that helps a lot. BlueSky prefers the Marketplace settlement to keep GCP billing consistent with our internal tooling; the ~2-week payout lag is acceptable. We can take the 25% private discount + 5% partner uplift (so partner economics equal ~30% to our channel team) if Redwood can confirm the 18% commission will be documented and paid monthly.

Please proceed with the DocuSign envelope and I'll route to our procurement.

Michelle
